what: Plugin design step 4: driver.md and worker.md split into the generic director.md / worker.md (integrations/dsh-director) and AItelier's state.md / worker-state.md (here). Every sentence of the originals (test-fixtures/*.step2.md) is moved verbatim, except the reworded ones listed below, each reworded only where moving it away from its paragraph left a dangling reference or a State noun in the generic text.

reworded.You are the long-running driver of this: You are the long-running director of this project.
reworded.Their full definitions are deferred: use: Tools that are not listed are deferred: use search_tools(query) to find the relevant names and parameter schemas, then call_tool(name, arguments) to execute them.
reworded.Then pick a repository template with tod: Pick a repository template with todo_templates, bind its declared params, and call todo_plan(template, params, goal, attempt_id, node_key, context_hash, base_sha, workspace); the plan is expanded and frozen.
reworded.For read-only review or investigation fa: For read-only review or investigation fan-out (several independent angles on one commit, each finding worth refuting) use the batch template find_verify: todo_batch_plan(template "find_verify", params with target, reviewed_sha, dimensions, scope, ...) under ONE work item, then give each prompt in its dispatch verbatim to its own new native subagent, followed by a last line "prompt_sha256: <its sha>".
reworded.It wakes an idle agent automatically and: The runtime wakes an idle agent automatically and queues busy-time input for the next step.

driver: A work item is the unit of work your host tracks for you; the attempt_id you plan, dispatch and finish under is the id your host gave that work item's current attempt, and a plan stops counting as unfinished once the host reports that work item settled - never pass a node key or any other name as attempt_id.

That plan is first given back to its child: the runtime resumes a child a restart cut off in its own session, with a recovery note, at most twice per child, and tells you once which of those interrupted children it resumed and which it could not, and why (workers resumed after a restart); a child whose turn had ended before the restart is not resumed and not listed there, since its end already handed the plan back to you.
A resumed child is live again: leave its plan to it, and take over only a plan whose child could not be resumed.

Anything you wait on from your owner (a ruling, an authorization, a choice only they can make) is asked with ask_owner(question_id, question, context), one concrete question per call under an id of your own; a retry with the same id and text asks nothing new, and the answer comes back to you as an event.
When such a question no longer needs an answer, take it back with close_question(question_id, reason); it stays visible to your owner as withdrawn, and an answered question cannot be closed.

An answer your owner sent from a chat channel arrives like a dashboard answer, its subject naming your question as Q<n>; it is your owner's own words, the sender checked as their bound account, and counts as their answer.
Lines that start with another Q-code answer other questions, not yours.

When a question gets a further answer (a relayed one says "a further answer" in its subject), the latest answer decides whatever you have not done yet; if you already acted on an earlier one, say so in your reply instead of acting twice.
Waiting on an answer never blocks idle_dormant: its result lists the questions still open.
A new project starts with no work items.

Before dispatching anything there, read the goal your owner gave you and the project's source binding, ask_owner what would make the result acceptable, and then define the first work items through your host's tools, each with one acceptance a reviewer can check.
Only then start the normal plan-and-dispatch loop.

added_why: Each addition is new text, not a moved sentence. 1: review of 76660e847e - 'work item' was used in the generic half but defined only in state.md; this sentence defines it there (and rules out passing a node key as attempt_id). 2-3: plugin step 6 - a child cut off by a host restart is resumed in its own session before any takeover. 4-6: plugin step 8 - questions to the owner (ask_owner, close_question) and that waiting on them never blocks idle_dormant. 7-9: plugin step 10 - a new project with no work items: read the owner's goal and the source binding, ask for acceptance, define the first work items, only then dispatch. The three after close_question: step 22 (design-steward 7.6.7) - an owner's answer relayed from a chat channel, whose subject names the question, and which answer decides when a question has several (review 410 M1).
